events.title: Russian invasion of Ukraine
events.description: Russia invades Ukraine. Brent tops $100 for the first time since 2014 and European stock markets fall by about 4%.

events.title: Fed raises rates by 0.75 point
events.description: The Fed raises its benchmark rate by three-quarters of a point to a 1.5%–1.75% range, its most aggressive hike since 1994.

events.title: Bank of Canada raises its rate by 1 point
events.description: The Bank of Canada raises its policy rate by 100 basis points to 2½%, choosing to front-load its increases.

events.title: Powell's Jackson Hole speech
events.description: Powell warns the Fed will need to keep a restrictive policy for some time to restore price stability. The S&P 500 falls 3.37% and the Nasdaq 3.94%.

events.title: Hotter-than-expected US inflation (August CPI)
events.description: A hotter-than-expected August inflation report revives fears of an aggressive Fed. The S&P 500 falls 4.32%, the Nasdaq 5.16% and NVIDIA 9.5%.

events.title: US controls on advanced chips to China
events.description: The Bureau of Industry and Security restricts China's access to advanced chips and to semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

events.title: Silicon Valley Bank failure
events.description: SVB says it must raise $2.25 billion after a $1.8 billion loss on its bonds; its stock falls 60% the next day and regulators shut the bank on March 10. The regional bank ETF loses 8%, then 4%.

events.title: OPEC+ surprise production cut
events.description: OPEC+ unexpectedly announces output cuts of about 1.16 million barrels per day. Brent gains 6.31% to $84.93, its best session since March 2022.

events.title: China requires licences for gallium and germanium exports
events.description: China announces export licences for gallium and germanium, two metals used in technology manufacturing.

events.title: Hamas attack on Israel (first trading day)
events.description: First trading day after the October 7 attack: oil jumps about 4 to 5%, gold and bonds rise.

events.title: US tightens AI-chip export curbs on China
events.description: The Commerce Department widens its controls to also block cut-down AI chips bound for China, such as NVIDIA's H800 and A800. NVIDIA closes down about 5%.

events.title: BP and shipping lines pause Red Sea transits
events.description: Amid Houthi attacks on ships, BP and shipping lines including Maersk and MSC pause Red Sea transits.

events.title: Iran's first direct attack on Israel
events.description: On Saturday night Iran launches drones and missiles at Israel, the vast majority intercepted. On Monday the S&P 500 loses 1.2% and the VIX closes at its highest since October, but oil settles lower and rising yields also weigh.

events.title: Threat of tougher chip curbs and Trump's Taiwan remarks
events.description: Bloomberg reports that Washington is weighing a sweeping rule (FDPR) against equipment makers that export to China, and Trump says Taiwan ought to pay the US for its defense. ASML falls 11% in Amsterdam and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF more than 7%.

events.title: Iranian missile strike on Israel
events.description: Iran fires missiles at Israel during the trading session; WTI crude spikes and the S&P 500 energy sector gains more than 2%. The S&P 500 falls 0.93% and the Nasdaq 1.53%.

events.title: Threat of 25% tariffs on Canada and Mexico
events.description: President-elect Trump vows an executive order on Jan. 20 imposing 25% tariffs on all goods from Canada and Mexico, plus an extra 10% on China. The US dollar rises more than 2% against the peso and hits a four-year high against the Canadian dollar.

events.title: US curbs on high-bandwidth memory chips and 140 entities
events.description: Washington adds 140 entities to its export restrictions and curbs high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips and 24 types of chipmaking tools bound for China.

events.title: DeepSeek AI shock
events.description: A low-cost Chinese AI model triggers a rout in chip stocks: NVIDIA falls 17% in one session.

events.title: US tariff orders on Canada, Mexico and China
events.description: Orders of February 1: 25% on Canada and Mexico (10% on Canadian energy) and 10% on China. First trading day on February 3.

events.title: 25% tariffs on Canada take effect
events.description: US tariffs on Canada take effect; Canada retaliates with 25% on $30 billion of imports. The TSX hits a near two-month low.

events.title: "Liberation Day" reciprocal tariffs
events.description: Announced on April 2 after the close: a 10% baseline tariff and reciprocal tariffs of 11 to 50%. Biggest four-day drop in five years.

events.title: 90-day pause on reciprocal tariffs
events.description: Positive shock: the 90-day pause sends the S&P 500 up 9.5%, its biggest one-day gain since 2008.

events.title: License required for NVIDIA H20 chips to China
events.description: NVIDIA discloses a $5.5 billion charge tied to exports of its H20 chips, which now need a license for China; AMD expects an $800 million hit. NVIDIA drops 7% and the Nasdaq more than 3%.

events.title: Israeli strikes on Iran
events.description: Israel strikes Iranian nuclear and military sites: oil gains between 7 and 13% during the session.

events.title: Trump letter: 35% tariff on Canada
events.description: In a letter posted on Thursday, Trump raises tariffs on Canadian imports to 35% from Aug. 1, on top of sectoral tariffs, and threatens more if Ottawa retaliates.

events.title: Threat of 100% tariffs on China
events.description: After China's rare-earth restrictions, a threat of 100% tariffs: the Nasdaq 100 loses 3.5% and crypto assets more than 9%.

events.title: End of trade talks with Canada
events.description: Washington ends trade talks with Canada after an Ontario advertisement quoting Ronald Reagan.

events.title: Greenland-linked tariffs on eight NATO countries
events.description: On a Saturday, Trump announces 10% tariffs from Feb. 1, rising to 25% on June 1, on eight NATO members until Greenland is sold to the US. When Wall Street reopens, the S&P 500 loses 2.06%, its worst session since October, and the dollar falls.

events.title: Supreme Court strikes down IEEPA tariffs
events.description: In a 6-3 ruling, the Supreme Court holds that IEEPA does not authorize the president to impose tariffs, voiding the reciprocal and drug-trafficking duties. That evening Trump signs a 10% global tariff (Section 122) limited to 150 days.

events.title: US–Israeli strikes on Iran
events.description: Strikes on Saturday, February 28; risk to the Strait of Hormuz. First trading day on March 2: oil jumps and stocks fall.

events.title: Two-week US–Iran ceasefire
events.description: Less than two hours before his 8 p.m. ET deadline, Trump agrees to a two-week ceasefire that allows safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The next day WTI plunges more than 16% to $94.41, its biggest one-day drop since April 2020.

events.title: US–Iran deal to end the war
events.description: Late on Sunday, Trump says a deal with Iran is complete and authorizes the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. On Monday the S&P 500 gains 1.65%, the Nasdaq 3.07% and US crude falls about 4.9% to $80.75.

events.title: US declines to extend CUSMA
events.description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer says the United States will not renew CUSMA in its current form. The agreement, which does not expire until 2036, is therefore not extended to 2042.

events.title: Collapse of the US–Iran ceasefire
events.description: After attacks on three commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and US strikes on Tuesday, Trump says on Wednesday that the ceasefire is over. Brent jumps more than 5% and the Dow falls 1.09%.

events.title: 50% Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods
events.description: Three Section 338 proclamations each impose a 50% tariff on Canadian imports, from wine to hockey sticks and cement, with no exemption for CUSMA-compliant goods, 30 days after signing.

events.title: Talks collapse: 50% tariffs on Canada take effect
events.description: After trade talks collapse, 50% tariffs apply from Saturday to about US$20 billion of Canadian goods, and Trump threatens 50% tariffs on Canadian vehicles, parts and steel from Jan. 1. The TSX closes higher, but the Canadian dollar slips to 72.24 US cents from 72.67.

events.title: Attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline
events.description: Drones launched from Iraq damage the East-West pipeline, with a capacity of 7 million barrels per day, which lets Saudi Arabia bypass the Strait of Hormuz; Riyadh shuts it as a precaution. Oil, back above $100 that week, ends the week more than 8% higher.

hedge_compare.method: Unhedged: your mix with SPY converted to Canadian dollars every day at the Bank of Canada rate (the engine’s own path, real data). Hedged stand-in (an assumption): the same mix with SPY’s line on its US-dollar returns, as if the USD/CAD move were removed, the way a CAD-hedged S&P 500 fund such as XSP is built. No hedging cost or gain is counted (a real hedge pays or earns the gap between the two currencies’ interest rates), so this is a stand-in, never XSP’s own record. Hedged like XSP (hedged_carry, an assumption): the same stand-in plus that carry, as a currency forward books it: each day the Bank of Canada target less the US effective federal funds rate known the day before, accrued by calendar day (a cost while US rates are higher). XSP’s fees, its monthly hedge resets and its tracking are not counted.

scenarios.method: A scenario you build, not a forecast. Each holding’s sensitivity to the 7 factors is measured on weekly returns in Canadian dollars from 2021-11 to the decision date (least squares with light ridge shrinkage; a holding that is itself a factor moves one for one with it). The engine is linear: a holding’s move is the sum of its sensitivities times the shocks, applied at once to today’s value (no path, no rebalancing, a holding cannot lose more than all of it); the mix’s move is the weighted sum. Preset sizes are measured moves from the record; the factors a preset does not name move with it as they did on average week to week (the measured co-movement). What the 7 factors do not explain (a company’s own news) is outside the engine: the check replays real windows, with sensitivities measured on data that includes them (in sample), and shows the gap. A fall closer to your floor than the widest gap for that mix is too close to call: the engine cannot tell the two sides apart.
